title: Merge sort body runtime
statement: Let a program contain the prescribed sorting, halving, merging, and copying procedures, and let the space limit be at most the word limit, with one also at most the word limit. Let $L$ be a list of integers represented in memory on the segment beginning at $a$, with $a+|L|\le fr$ and $fr+|L|$ at most the space limit. Suppose $d$ is below the depth limit, and that for every starting address $a'$, list $L'$, and memory $\mu'$, if $1<|L|$, $2|L'|\le |L|+1$, $L'$ is represented in $\mu'$ on the segment beginning at $a'$, and $a'+|L'|\le fr$, then the sorting procedure at depth $d+1$, started with length $|L'|$, address $a'$, and free address $fr$, terminates within $\mathrm{sortTime}(|L'|)$ and leaves memory in which the segment beginning at $a'$ is sorted and the required memory outside that segment is preserved. Then the sorting body at depth $d$, started with length $|L|$, address $a$, free address $fr$, and memory $\mu$, terminates within $\mathrm{sortTime}(|L|)$ and leaves memory in which the segment beginning at $a$ is sorted and the required memory outside it is preserved.
hypotheses_covered: Program contains the prescribed sort, half, merge, and copy procedure bodies
Space limit is at most the word limit
One is at most the word limit
Initial memory represents L on the segment beginning at a

Induction hypothesis: for every a', L', and μ', if 1 < |L|, 2|L'| ≤ |L| + 1, μ' represents L' at a', and a' + |L'| ≤ fr, then the sort procedure at depth d + 1 meets the stated time and sorted-memory condition
